text.p: Eurotunnel Plc/SA's plans for a sleeper service are being reviewed because some of Britain's mainline tracks may not be able to cope with the necessary power demands, the Financial Times reported on Monday.

"We are worried that if everyone went to the loo (lavatory) or had a shower at the same time the train would stop," the newpaper quoted Adam Mills, new chief executive of London & Continental Railways as saying.
London & Continental Railways (LCR) is the private consortium which won the contract to operate the Eurostar high-speed passenger train services through the Channel Tunnel in June.

The newspaper said that the problem line was the main line from London to Birmingham and Glasgow in Scotland -- the first line on which the sleeper service to the Continent is supposed to be introduced.
But LCR's Mills said the problems were solveable, adding that the sleepers were not being cancelled.
"There is a political desire for sleepers, but we are reviewing the whole operation," he was reported as saying. "There are horrendous technical problems."
